Review the backup replication setting if a single-region requirement applies, since cross-region replication is enabled by default. Metadata such as account names and billing records is stored centrally regardless of the data region. [1]

Open the revisions page for the service and identify the last revision that was healthy. Select roll back on that revision. Traffic moves within roughly thirty seconds and no rebuild takes place. If the release included a database migration, roll the migration back before the service, or the older code will encounter a schema it does not expect. Rollback restores the container image and its configuration together. [2]

If that does not resolve it, reply to this message and a support engineer will pick it up.

response_body:
Thanks for getting in touch.

Pin your dependencies with exact versions and commit the lock file. Unpinned dependencies are the cause in the large majority of cases of this kind. Compare the runtime version declared in your build configuration against the version you use locally. Clear the build cache from the settings page and trigger a fresh build to rule out a corrupted artefact. Build logs retain the full resolution output for thirty days, which is usually enough to identify which version changed. [1]

If that does not resolve it, reply to this message and a support engineer will pick it up.
